title: Neuroimaging in the era of biologically defined Alzheimer's disease and disease-modifying therapy
title_zh: 生物学定义的阿尔茨海默病与疾病修饰治疗时代的神经影像学
abstract: Disease-modifying therapies and biomarker-based diagnostic frameworks will fundamentally altered the clinical diagnosis and management of Alzheimer's disease. Diagnosis is increasingly anchored in the biological evidence of pathology rather than clinical presentation alone, with implications for treatment eligibility, prognosis, and monitoring. In clinical practice, patients with memory complaints can present with complex mixed pathologies that develop across the lifespan. Brain imaging, particularly MRI and PET, plays a crucial role in visualising these cumulative abnormalities. With Alzheimer's disease-specific therapies now available in many regions of the world, amyloid PET plays a central role in establishing Alzheimer's disease diagnosis, determining eligibility for amyloid-targeting therapies, and quantifying treatment-related amyloid clearance. In settings where available, tau PET informs biological stage, prognosis, and clinical heterogeneity. MRI remains indispensable for differential diagnosis, the assessment of comorbid and vascular pathology, and monitoring for complications, particularly amyloid-related imaging abnormalities. Technological advances-including quantitative imaging, artificial intelligence, accelerated acquisition, and workflow optimisation-are improving reliability, efficiency, and access to these tools. Neuroimaging is now a cornerstone of Alzheimer's disease care and a crucial discriminator tool for characterising brain injury across the lifespan. With emerging fluid biomarkers, neuroimaging supports accurate diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring.
abstract_zh: 疾病修饰治疗和基于生物标志物的诊断框架将从根本上改变阿尔茨海默病的临床诊断与管理。诊断正日益以病理的生物学证据为基础，而非仅凭临床表现，这对治疗资格、预后和监测产生深远影响。在临床实践中，伴有记忆障碍的患者可能呈现跨生命周期发展的复杂混合病理。脑影像，尤其是MRI和PET，在可视化这些累积异常方面发挥关键作用。随着阿尔茨海默病特异性治疗在全球许多地区可用，淀粉样蛋白PET在确立阿尔茨海默病诊断、确定淀粉样蛋白靶向治疗的适应症以及量化治疗相关淀粉样蛋白清除方面起核心作用。在可用的环境中，tau PET可提供生物学阶段、预后和临床异质性信息。MRI仍然是鉴别诊断、评估共病和血管病变以及监测并发症（尤其是淀粉样相关影像异常）的不可或缺工具。技术进步——包括定量影像、人工智能、加速采集和工作流程优化——正在提升这些工具的可靠性、效率和可及性。神经影像学已成为阿尔茨海默病护理的基石，也是跨生命周期表征脑损伤的关键鉴别工具。随着流体生物标志物的出现，神经影像学支持精准诊断、预后评估和治疗监测。
